subject: SIG: BYOK onboarding, HSM attestations and key rotation details
messages:
From: Claire Xu <claire.xu@finpay.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: security_ops@finpay.com
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up — BYOK, key exportability, HSM evidence

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for taking the initial SIG packet; we've started mapping questions to our procurement checklist. A few items we need from Redwood to finalize the crypto section (SIG v2025):

- Can you confirm whether production customer keys are ever exportable in plaintext from your platform? We need a short affirmative/negative and a description of the technical control.
- For BYOK: what is the onboarding flow (import vs envelope encryption), and do you support customer-supplied keys that remain under our KMS/HSM control?
- HSM vendor and certification level (FIPS 140-2/3 L3 vs L4) and whether you can provide a vendor attestation letter.
- Key rotation cadence defaults and whether rotation can be customer-driven (API) with rotation logs retained for 7+ years.

If possible, attach a short BYOK runbook or any evidence we can upload to the SIG portal. We're on a tight timeline to close procurement by Sep 10.

Best,
Claire
Claire Xu
Lead InfoSec Manager, FinPay
Claire.xu@finpay.com

--

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Xu <claire.xu@finpay.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — BYOK, key exportability, HSM evidence

Claire —

Appreciate the detailed list. Short answers up front, followed by brief notes and attached artifacts: redwood_byok_guide_2027-08.pdf (BYOK runbook) and hsm_vendor_letter_2027-07.pdf (vendor attestation).

- Exportable keys: NO — customer master keys (CMKs) used for encryption at rest are configured as non-exportable by default. We use envelope encryption: app data keys (DEKs) are generated per-tenant and wrapped by the CMK; CMKs are protected in an HSM and marked non-exportable.

- BYOK onboarding: we support two modes: (1) Customer-supplied external key material imported into a customer-specific KMS instance with HSM-backed key wrapping; (2) Envelope/BYOK where customer provides a root key that wraps platform CMKs. Both options preserve customer control; import is performed through an authenticated, audited import API or via a secure key ceremony if the customer requests. See attached BYOK runbook for step-by-step.

- HSM vendor & certifications: We currently use Thales Luna HSMs (deployment-managed for hosted customers; for Dedicated/Private we support customer-run HSM stacks). Thales HSMs are FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated; we maintain vendor attestation letters (attached).

- Rotation & logs: Default rotation cadence for intermediate DEKs is 90 days; CMKs are rotated per customer policy (supporting manual API-driven rotation or scheduled rotation). Rotation operations emit a signed audit event containing timestamp, initiating principal, and key version IDs. Audit logs are retained in the customer tenant for 7 years (configurable) and are exportable via our audit API.

Next steps: I can provide a short excerpt that maps exactly to SIG question IDs (e.g., the key exportability statement for Q12.3.5) and upload the artifacts to the Drive link you shared. If you'd like, Hannah or Grace can join a 30-minute call this week to walk through the runbook and the attestation.

Proposed times: Thu Aug 2 (actually Sep 2) 10:00–10:30 PT or Fri Sep 3 14:00–14:30 PT. Let me know what works.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Security Lead — Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood_byok_guide_2027-08.pdf (PDF, 12 pages), hsm_vendor_letter_2027-07.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)

From: Claire Xu <claire.xu@finpay.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: security_ops@finpay.com
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2027 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — BYOK, key exportability, HSM evidence

Jordan — thanks, that was helpful. A couple follow-ups from our engineering & crypto review:

1) Can you confirm whether the HSM-backed CMKs are hardware keys that are strictly non-exportable (no key material leave HSM in any deployment mode)? Our procurement team needs precise language to include in the contract.
2) Is the Thales attestation you provided an up-to-date letter covering the exact cluster we will be provisioned to (or is it a generic vendor attestation)? We may need a cluster-specific statement for our compliance team.
3) For BYOK import: is there an option where the customer retains the wrapping key in their own cloud KMS and Redwood never sees the unwrapped CMK?
4) Regarding audit logs: can your signed audit events be verified by a public key we hold (i.e., can you sign events with a Redwood verification key and provide the public key so we can validate integrity)?

If you can provide contract-grade wording for (1) and (3) and a timeline for cluster-specific attestation (if required), we can move the SIG answers forward. We also plan to request a 3rd-party pen test report — can you share the most recent one or a redaction?

Best,
Claire

--
(Please do not include full pen test binaries; a summary or redacted report is fine.)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Xu <claire.xu@finpay.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — BYOK, key exportability, HSM evidence

Claire —

Thanks — answers below, and I've attached a short checklist for BYOK onboarding (byok_onboarding_checklist.xlsx). We'll also open JIRA SUP-9412 to track the attestation request.

1) Contract wording (suggested): "Customer master keys used to protect tenant encryption keys are cryptographic keys generated or imported into an HSM-backed key store and are configured as non-exportable. Under normal operation, key material does not leave the HSM in plaintext and cannot be extracted via software interfaces."

2) Attestation letter: the attached vendor letter is a current Thales vendor attestation covering our managed HSM fleet. For Dedicated/Private deployments we can obtain a cluster-specific attestation; typical turnaround is 5–10 business days once we have customer cluster identifiers and an executed non-disclosure addendum (NDA) with the vendor. We can initiate that upon your confirmation.

3) BYOK import modes: Yes — we support an option where the customer retains the wrapping key in their own cloud KMS and Redwood never has access to the unwrapped CMK. That pattern is commonly used for high-control customers (BYOK-without-import). We document the sequence in step 3 of the attached runbook; it uses an envelope-wrapping flow where Redwood only stores wrapped keys and holds no plaintext key material.

4) Signed audit events: We can publish a short-lived public verification key (or a rotating key pair) and include a signature in each exported audit bundle. Verification guidance and public key distribution is described in our audit API docs (link above). If you need an HSM-backed signing certificate bound to our attestation, we can discuss scope and timeframe.

Pen test: we can provide a redacted executive summary and remediation log (redaction to remove customer-identifying artifacts). I'll coordinate with our security operations team and upload the summary to the Drive folder.

Logistics: Hannah will coordinate the SUP-9412 ticket and propose concrete times for a 30-minute BYOK workshop during the week of Sep 6. Grace will prepare contract-grade statements for (1) and (3) and put them in a signed PDF we can attach to the SIG portal.

If you want contract language now, here's a compact clause you can paste into the SIG portal: 

"Redwood Inference: Customer master keys (CMKs) are HSM-protected and configured non-exportable; envelope encryption is used for data keys. Customers opting for BYOK may choose to import key material under a controlled import API or retain wrapping keys in their own KMS; in either case Redwood does not retain unwrapped key material."

Happy to answer anything else.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Security Lead — Redwood Inference

Attachments: byok_onboarding_checklist.xlsx (Excel), [pending] pen_test_summary_redacted.pdf (to be uploaded)
